Q320449.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcestis or Alceste, was a princess of Iolcus known for her love of her husband. Her life story was described by Pseudo-Apollodorus in his Bibliotheca, and a version of her death and return from the dead was also popularized by Euripides' tragedy Alcestis.

Q320660.label: Chrysaor
Q320660.lead: In Greek mythology, Chrysaor was the brother of the winged horse Pegasus, often depicted as a young man, the son of Poseidon and Medusa, born when Perseus decapitated the Gorgon Medusa.

Q321298.label: Aegina
Q321298.description: nymph, eponym of the island Aegina
Q321298.lead: Aegina was a figure of Greek mythology, the nymph of the island that bears her name, Aegina, lying in the Saronic Gulf between Attica and the Peloponnesos. The archaic Temple of Aphaea, the "Invisible Goddess", on the island was later subsumed by the cult of Athena.

Q321541.label: Meleager
Q321541.description: son of Oeneus in Greek mythology, king of Calydon
Q321541.lead: Meleager was a hero in Greek mythology, venerated in his temenos at Calydon in Aetolia. He was famed as the host of the Calydonian boar hunt in the epic tradition that was reworked by Homer, and was also mentioned as one of the Argonauts.

Q322639.label: Neoptolemus
Q322639.lead: In Greek mythology, Neoptolemus, originally called Pyrrhus at birth (Πύρρος, Pýrrhos, 'red'), was the son of the mythical warrior Achilles and the princess Deidamia, and the brother of Oneiros. He became the progenitor of the ruling dynasty of the Molossians of ancient Epirus.

Q326767.label: Thaumas
Q326767.lead: In Greek mythology, Thaumas or Thaumant was a sea god, son of Pontus and Gaia, and the full brother of Nereus, Phorcys, Ceto and Eurybia.

Q3268516.label: Lycus
Q3268516.description: Greek mythical character, son of Dascylus

Q329690.label: Cleodaeus
Q329690.lead: In Greek mythology, Cleodaeus was one of the Heracleidae, a grandson of Heracles. He was the son of Heracles's eldest son Hyllus and Iole of Oechalia.

Q330584.label: Amphiaraus
Q330584.lead: Amphiaraus or Amphiaraos was in Greek mythology the son of Oicles, a seer, and one of the leaders of the Seven against Thebes. Amphiaraus at first refused to go with Adrastus on this expedition against Thebes as he foresaw the death of everyone who joined the expedition.

Q331327.label: Telamon
Q331327.description: one of the Argonauts of Jason, in Greek mythology
Q331327.lead: Telamon in Greek mythology was the son of King Aeacus of Aegina, and Endeïs, a mountain nymph. The elder brother of Peleus, Telamon sailed alongside Jason as one of his Argonauts, and was present at the hunt for the Calydonian Boar.

Q332324.label: Laomedon
Q332324.lead: In Greek mythology, Laomedon was a Trojan king, son of Ilus and thus nephew of Ganymede and Assaracus. Laomedon was variously identified with different parents and siblings, as well as numerous children, including Priam and Tithonus.

Q332752.label: Hylas
Q332752.description: mythical character, companion of Heracles abducted by nymphs
Q332752.lead: In classical mythology, Hylas was a youth who served Heracles (Roman Hercules) as companion and servant. His abduction by water nymphs was a theme of ancient art, and has been an enduring subject for Western art in the classical tradition.

Q333658.label: Absyrtus
Q333658.lead: In Greek mythology, Absyrtus or Apsyrtus Ancient Greek: Άψυρτος) was a Colchian prince and brother or half-brother of Medea. He was involved in Jason's escape with the golden fleece from Colchis.

Q334817.label: Polynices
Q334817.lead: In Greek mythology, Polynices (also Polyneices) was the son of Oedipus and either Jocasta or Euryganeia, and the brother of Eteocles, Antigone, and Ismene. When Oedipus discovered that he had killed his father and married his mother, he blinded himself and left Thebes, leaving Polynices and Eteocles to rule jointly.

Q336428.label: Hellen
Q336428.lead: In Greek mythology, Hellen is the eponymous progenitor of the Hellenes. He is the son of Deucalion (or Zeus) and Pyrrha, and the father of three sons, Dorus, Xuthus, and Aeolus.

Q3378668.label: Phaethon
Q3378668.description: son of Eos by Cephalus or Tithonus in Greek mythology
Q3378668.lead: In Greek mythology, Phaethon was a son of Eos by Cephalus of Athens or Tithonus, born in Syria.

Q34041.label: Icarus
Q34041.description: Greek mythological figure, son of Daedalus
Q34041.lead: In Greek mythology, Icarus was the son of the master craftsman Daedalus, the architect of the labyrinth of Crete, and his wife Naucrate. After Theseus, king of Athens and enemy of King Minos, escaped from the labyrinth, Minos suspected that Icarus and Daedalus had revealed the labyrinth's secrets and thus imprisoned the two, either in a large tower overlooking the ocean or in the labyrinth itself, depending upon the account.

Q3411223.label: Pylas
Q3411223.lead: In Greek mythology, Pylas, also called Pylon or Pylos, was a king of Megara and successor of his father Cteson, son of Lelex.

Q34201.label: Zeus
Q34201.description: Greek god of the sky and king of the gods
Q34201.lead: Zeus is the supreme deity of the Greek pantheon. He is a sky and thunder god in ancient Greek religion and mythology, who rules as king of the gods on Mount Olympus.

Q342279.label: Hippocoon
Q342279.description: king of Sparta, son of Oebalus
Q342279.lead: In Greek mythology, Hippocoön was a Spartan king.

Q342343.label: Perieres
Q342343.lead: In Greek mythology, Perieres was the 'overbold' king of Messene, an ancient polis in southern Peloponnese.

Q3483923.label: Sylea
Q3483923.description: daughter of Corinthus in Greek mythology

Q3499887.label: Phoebe
Q3499887.description: Daughter of Leucippus, mythical figure honored at Sparta
Q3499887.lead: In Greek mythology, Phoebe was a Messenian princess.

Q35500.label: Aphrodite
Q35500.description: Greek goddess of love, beauty, pleasure, and procreation
Q35500.lead: Aphrodite is an ancient Greek goddess associated with love and beauty. Aphrodite's main cult centers were Cythera, Cyprus, Corinth, and Athens.

Q3618707.label: Antimache
Q3618707.lead: In Greek mythology, Antimache was the queen of Tiryns as wife of King Eurystheus, who tasked Heracles with his Labors.

Q3622209.label: Arete
Q3622209.description: person in Greek mythology, wife of Alcinous
Q3622209.lead: In Greek mythology, Queen Arete of Scheria was the wife of Alcinous and mother of Nausicaa and Laodamas.

Q3625559.label: Strymon
Q3625559.lead: In Greek mythology, Strymon was a river-god and son of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-wife Tethys. He was a king of Thrace.

Q362738.label: Taphius
Q362738.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q362738.lead: In Greek mythology, Taphius founded the city Taphos on the island of the same name, and was its king. He also gave his name to the Taphians, a people that inhabited Taphos and nearby islands, which formed part of Odysseus's kingdom at the time of the Trojan War.

Q3636218.label: Baton
Q3636218.lead: Baton is a character from Greek mythology. He was said to have been the charioteer of the hero Amphiaraus, and that both belonged to the house of the legendary seer Melampus.

Q368423.label: Stheneboea
Q368423.description: wife of King Proetus in Greek mythology
Q368423.lead: In Greek mythology, Stheneboea also called Antea in Homer (Ancient Greek: Ἄντεια, romanized: Ánteia), is the daughter of Iobates, king in Lycia. She was the queen consort of Proetus, joint-king in the Argolid along with Acrisius, having his seat at Tiryns.

Q3699000.label: Cteatus
Q3699000.description: son of Actor son of Phorbas in Greek mythology

Q3705305.label: Demophon
Q3705305.description: king of Elaeus in Greek mythology
Q3705305.lead: Demophon is a king of Elaeus in Thrace from ancient Greek and Roman mythology. In order to combat a deadly disease that plagued his city, Demophon sacrificed the daughters of noblemen, an act that enraged Mastusius, the father of one of the victims, who then sought revenge.

Q3706015.label: Dexamenus
Q3706015.description: mythical king of Olenus in Achaea

Q371206.label: Astypalaea
Q371206.description: lover of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q371206.lead: In Greek mythology, Astypalaea or Astypalaia or Astypale was a Phoenician princess as the daughter of King Phoenix and Perimede, daughter of Oeneus; thus she was the sister of Europa. In some accounts, her mother was called Telephe and her siblings were Peirus and again Europe.

Q37122.label: Athena
Q37122.description: goddess of wisdom and war in ancient Greek religion and mythology
Q37122.lead: Athena or Athene, often given the epithet Pallas, is an ancient Greek goddess associated with wisdom, warfare, and handicraft who was later syncretised with the Roman goddess Minerva and Etruscan Menrva. Athena was regarded as the patron and protectress of various cities across Greece, particularly the city of Athens, from which she most likely received her name.

Q371545.label: Megaera
Q371545.description: one of the Erinyes or Furies
Q371545.lead: Megaera is one of the Erinyes, Eumenides or "Furies" in classical mythology. Bibliotheca Classica states "According to the most received opinions, they were three in number, Tisiphone, "Megaera ...

Q37340.label: Apollo
Q37340.description: god in Greek and later Roman mythology
Q37340.lead: Apollo is one of the Olympian deities in ancient Greek religion and mythology. His numerous functions include light, healing, prophecy, music, poetry, and archery.

Q3744926.label: Phylas
Q3744926.description: in Greek mythology, king of Ephyra, a descendant of Dryopes

Q3792157.label: Iphianassa
Q3792157.description: daughter of Proetus in Greek mythology

Q38012.label: Hera
Q38012.description: Greek goddess, wife and sister of Zeus
Q38012.lead: In ancient Greek religion, Hera is the goddess of marriage, women, and family, and the protector of women during childbirth. In Greek mythology, she is queen among the twelve Olympians on Mount Olympus, sister and wife of Zeus, and daughter of the Titans Cronus and Rhea.

Q381459.label: Agave
Q381459.description: daughter of Cadmus in Greek mythology
Q381459.lead: In Greek mythology, Agave, was the daughter of Cadmus and a princess of Thebes. She is most well known for her role in the myths surrounding her nephew, Dionysus, god of wine.

Q381931.label: Aethlius
Q381931.description: son of Zeus in Greek mythology
Q381931.lead: Aethlius or Aithlios or Aethnos was, in Greek mythology, the first king of Elis.

Q3854654.label: Menesthius
Q3854654.description: son of Spercheus in Greek mythology

Q3860293.label: Molorchus
Q3860293.description: helper of Heracles in Greek mythology
Q3860293.lead: Molorchus was a day labourer at Cleonae who hosted Heracles when he came on his way to Nemea to kill the Nemean lion.

Q3893378.label: Panopeus
Q3893378.description: son of Phocus in Greek mythology
Q3893378.lead: In Greek mythology, Panopeus was a son of Phocus by Asteria or Asterodia, and twin brother of Crisus. The two brothers were so inimical towards each other that they began fighting while still in their mother's womb, just like Proetus and Acrisius did.

Q3898964.label: Pelorus
Q3898964.description: one of the mythical Spartoi of Thebes

Q3899862.label: Periclymenus
Q3899862.description: son of Neleus in Greek mythology

Q390492.label: Agapenor
Q390492.description: son of Ancaeus in Greek mythology
Q390492.lead: In Greek mythology, Agapenor was a leader of the Arcadians in the Trojan War.

Q3907701.label: Poltys
Q3907701.description: mythical king and eponym of the Thracian city of Poltyobria
Q3907701.lead: Poltys is also a genus of spiders In Greek mythology, Poltys is a mythical king and eponym of the Thracian city of Poltyobria (or Poltymbria; also called Aenus), featured in Apollodorus's account of the story of the hero Heracles. Poltys and his brother Sarpedon are given as sons of the sea-god Poseidon.

Q391010.label: Chalciope
Q391010.lead: Chalciope, in Greek mythology, was a Colchian princess as the daughter of King Aeëtes. Acusilaus, Hesiod and Hesychius referred to her as Iophossa (Ιoφώσσης) while according to Pherecydes, she was called Euenia (Εύηνίαν).

Q391091.label: Pentheus
Q391091.description: mythical king of Thebes, son of Echion and Agave
Q391091.lead: In Greek mythology, Pentheus was a king of Thebes. His father was Echion, the wisest of the Spartoi.

Q391379.label: Achelous
Q391379.lead: Achelous (also Acheloos or Acheloios) was the god in ancient Greek religion and mythology associated with the Achelous River, the largest river in Greece. According to Hesiod, he was the son of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

Q3923920.label: Pronous
Q3923920.description: son of Phegeus in Greek mythology

Q392435.label: Aristaeus
Q392435.lead: Aristaeus was the mythological culture hero credited with the discovery of many rural useful arts and handicrafts, including beekeeping. He was the son of the huntress Cyrene and Apollo.

Q392631.label: Agenor
Q392631.description: mythical Phoenician king, father of Cadmus
Q392631.lead: Agenor was in Greek mythology and history a Phoenician king of Tyre or Sidon. The Greek historian Herodotus (c.

Q393186.label: Diomedes of Thrace
Q393186.description: son of Ares in Greek mythology
Q393186.lead: In Greek mythology, King Diomedes of Thrace was the son of Ares and Cyrene. He lived on the shores of the Black Sea ruling the warlike tribe of Bistones.

Q39503.label: Artemis
Q39503.description: goddess of the hunt and the wild in ancient Greek religion and mythology
Q39503.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Artemis is the goddess of hunting, the wilderness, wild animals, transitions, nature, vegetation, childbirth, care of children, and chastity. She was often said to roam the forests and mountains, attended by an entourage of nymphs.

Q398524.label: Philyra
Q398524.lead: In Greek mythology, Philyra or Phillyra was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

Q4002579.label: Udaeus
Q4002579.description: one of the mythical Spartoi of Thebes
Q4002579.lead: In Greek mythology, Udaeus was one of the Spartoi or men that grew forth from the dragon's teeth which Cadmus sowed at Thebes. The other four surviving Spartoi were Chthonius, Hyperenor, Pelorus, and Echion.

Q4024302.label: Zetes
Q4024302.description: son of Boreas in Greek mythology

Q404326.label: Aegimius
Q404326.description: mythical character, king of the Dorians
Q404326.lead: Aegimius was the Greek mythological ancestor of the Dorians, who is described as their king and lawgiver at the time when they were yet inhabiting the northern parts of Thessaly.

Q404844.label: Aegyptus
Q404844.description: son of Belus in Greek mythology
Q404844.lead: In Greek mythology, Aegyptus or Ægyptus was a legendary king of ancient Egypt. He was a descendant of the princess Io through his father Belus, and of the river-god Nilus as both the father of Achiroe, his mother and as a great, great-grandfather on his father's side.

Q406388.label: Aiolos
Q406388.description: hero ancestor of the Aeolians, son of Hellen
Q406388.lead: In Greek mythology, Aeolus or Aiolos was the son of Hellen, the ruler of Aeolia (later called Thessaly), and the eponym of the Aeolians, one of the four main tribes of the Greeks. According to the mythographer Apollodorus, Aeolus was the father of seven sons: Cretheus, Sisyphus, Athamas, Salmoneus, Deion, Magnes, Perieres, and five daughters: Canace, Alcyone, Pisidice, Calyce, and Perimede.

Q406443.label: Aepytus
Q406443.lead: In Greek mythology, Aepytus was the youngest son of Cresphontes the Heraclid, king of Messenia, and of Merope, the daughter of the Arcadian king Cypselus.

Q40730.label: Demeter
Q40730.description: Greek goddess of the harvest, grains, and agriculture
Q40730.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Demeter is the Olympian goddess of the harvest and agriculture, presiding over crops, grains, food, and the fertility of the earth. Although Demeter is mostly known as a grain goddess, she also appeared as a goddess of health, birth, and marriage, and had connections to the Underworld.

Q40901.label: Ares
Q40901.description: Greek god of war and combat
Q40901.lead: Ares is the Greek god of war and courage. He is one of the Twelve Olympians, and the son of Zeus and Hera.

Q409520.label: Aesacus
Q409520.description: son of Priam in Greek mythology
Q409520.lead: In Greek mythology, Aesacus or Aisakos was a son of King Priam of Troy. Aesacus sorrowed for the death of his wife or would-be lover, a daughter of the river Cebren, and was transformed into a seabird.

Q410082.label: Aeson
Q410082.description: father of Jason in Greek mythology
Q410082.lead: In Greek mythology, Aeson was a king of Iolcus in Thessaly. He was the father of the hero Jason.

Q41054.label: Epimetheus
Q41054.lead: In Greek mythology, Epimetheus is the brother of Prometheus, with the complementary pair serving as archetypal representations of mankind. Both are sons of the Titan Iapetus; while Prometheus ("forethought, or foresight") is portrayed as ingeniously clever, Epimetheus ("afterthought, or hindsight") is considered inept and foolish.

Q410748.label: Aetolus
Q410748.lead: Aetolus was, in Greek mythology, a son of Endymion, great-great-grandson of Deucalion, and a Naiad nymph (Neis), or Iphianassa.

Q41127.label: Poseidon
Q41127.description: one of the twelve Olympians presiding over the sea, storms, earthquakes and horses
Q41127.lead: Poseidon is one of the twelve Olympians in ancient Greek religion and mythology, presiding over the sea, storms, earthquakes and horses. He was the protector of seafarers and the guardian of many Hellenic cities and colonies.

Q4137657.label: Hesione
Q4137657.description: Greek mythical character, daughter of Laomedon
Q4137657.lead: In Greek mythology, Hesione was a Trojan princess.

Q41410.label: Hades
Q41410.description: god of the underworld in Greek mythology
Q41410.lead: Hades, in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous. Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

Q41419.label: Hestia
Q41419.description: Greek goddess of the hearth and the home
Q41419.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Hestia is the virgin goddess of the hearth and the home. In myth, she is the firstborn child of the Titans Cronus and Rhea, and one of the Twelve Olympians.

Q41484.label: Hermes
Q41484.description: Olympian god in Greek religion and mythology; the emissary and messenger of the gods; the god of trade, heraldry, merchants, commerce, roads, thieves, trickery, sports, travelers, and athletes; the son of Zeus and the Pleiad Maia
Q41484.lead: Hermes is an Olympian deity in ancient Greek religion and mythology considered the herald of the gods. He is also widely considered the protector of human heralds, travelers, thieves, merchants, and orators.

Q416384.label: Acastus
Q416384.lead: Acastus is a character in Greek mythology. He sailed with Jason and the Argonauts, and participated in the hunt for the Calydonian Boar.

Q41680.label: Dionysus
Q41680.description: ancient Greek god of winemaking and wine
Q41680.lead: In ancient Greek religion and myth, Dionysus is the god of wine-making, orchards, fruit, vegetation, fertility, festivity, insanity, ritual madness, religious ecstasy, and theatre. He was also known as Bacchus (Ancient Greek: Βάκχος Bacchos) by the Greeks (a name later adopted by the Romans) for a frenzy he is said to induce called baccheia.

Q41746.label: Achilles
Q41746.description: Greek mythological hero of the Trojan War
Q41746.lead: In Greek mythology, Achilles or Achilleus (Ancient Greek: Ἀχιλλεύς, romanized: Achilleús) was a hero of the Trojan War who was known as being the greatest of all the Greek warriors. The central character in Homer's Iliad, he was the son of the Nereid Thetis and Peleus, king of Phthia and famous Argonaut.

Q420269.label: Arges
Q420269.lead: Arges was one of the three Hesiodic Cyclopes in Greek mythology. He was elsewhere called Acmonides or Pyracmon.

Q423424.label: Actor
Q423424.description: king in Greek mythology, son of Phorbas

Q4300425.label: Molione
Q4300425.description: Mythological character, mother of the Moliones
Q4300425.lead: In Greek mythology, Molione or Moline (Μολίνη) was a member of the Aetolian royal family.

Q430157.label: Eryx
Q430157.description: in Greek mythology, king of the city Eryx in Sicily

Q431387.label: Deidamia
Q431387.description: Greek mythological figure, daughter of Lycomedes
Q431387.lead: In Greek mythology, Deidamia is a daughter of King Lycomedes, who lives on the island of Scyros. She marries Achilles, by whom she becomes the mother of Neoptolemus.

Q4347884.label: Pedias
Q4347884.description: mythological Greek character, wife of Kranaos
Q4347884.lead: In Greek mythology, Pedias was the Lacedamonian daughter of Mynes. She married the autochthonous King Cranaus who reigned in Athens and bore him three daughters: Cranaë, Cranaechme, and Atthis.

Q440422.label: Althaemenes
Q440422.description: son of Catreus in Greek mythology
Q440422.lead: In Greek mythology, Althaemenes or Althemenes was a Cretan prince as the only son of King Catreus of Crete. He was the brother of Apemosyne, Aerope and Clymene.

Q440440.label: Althaea
Q440440.lead: In Greek mythology, Althaea, also rendered Althea or Althaia, was queen of Calydon through her marriage to King Oeneus. Althaea appears in myths surrounding the fabled Calydonian boar hunt, and is infamous for murdering her son Meleager.

Q44204.label: Cronus
Q44204.description: ruler of the Titans in Greek mythology
Q44204.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Cronus, Cronos, or Kronos was the leader and youngest of the Titans, the children of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky). Cronus castrated and overthrew his father and then ruled during the mythological Golden Age until he himself was overthrown by his son, Zeus, and imprisoned in Tartarus.

Q44384.label: Hephaestus
Q44384.lead: Hephaestus is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes. In Greek mythology, Hephaestus was the son of Hera, either on her own or by her husband Zeus.

Q45967.label: Persephone
Q45967.description: Greek goddess of the seasons and the queen of the underworld; married with Hades
Q45967.lead: In ancient Greek mythology and religion, Persephone is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter. She became the queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, the king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.

Q461212.label: Dardanus
Q461212.description: mythological Greek character, son of Zeus
Q461212.lead: In Greek mythology, Dardanus was the founder of the city of Dardanus at the foot of Mount Ida in the Troad. Dardanus, a son of Zeus and the Pleiad Electra, was a significant figure in Greek mythology.

Q461439.label: Antiope
Q461439.description: Greek mythological figure; daughter of Nycteus and mother of Amphion
Q461439.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Antiope is the mother of the twin heroes Amphion and Zethus by Zeus the king of the gods. Although stated in early sources to be a daughter of the Boeotian river god Asopus, most authors made her a child of king Nycteus of Thebes.

Q463107.label: Autolycus
Q463107.description: son of Daedalion in Greek mythology
Q463107.lead: In Greek mythology, Autolycus was a robber who had the power to metamorphose or make invisible the things he stole. He had his residence on Mount Parnassus and was renowned among men for his cunning and oaths.

Q463865.label: Pleione
Q463865.lead: Pleione was an Oceanid nymph in Greek mythology and mother of the Pleiades. Pleione presided over the multiplication of the flocks, fitting, since the meaning of her name is: "to increase in number" (from the Greek word pleiôn πλεῖων "more").

Q463898.label: Laius
Q463898.description: mythological king of Thebes, father of Oedipus
Q463898.lead: In Greek mythology, King Laius ( L(A)Y-əs) or Laios of Thebes was a key personage in the Theban founding myth. Son of King Labdacus, Laius fathered Oedipus with Jocasta and was later killed by Oedipus, although Oedipus did not know Laius was his father at the time.

Q464091.label: Silenus
Q464091.description: figure in Greek mythology; tutor to Dionysus
Q464091.lead: In Greek mythology, Silenus was a companion and tutor to the wine god Dionysus. He is typically older than the satyrs of the Dionysian retinue (thiasos), and sometimes considerably older, in which case he may be referred to as a Papposilenus.

Q466866.label: Nessus
Q466866.lead: In Greek mythology, Nessus was a famous centaur who was killed by Heracles, and whose poisoned blood in turn killed Heracles. He was the son of Centauros.

Q47231.label: Odysseus
Q47231.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Odysseus, also known by the Latin variant Ulysses (UK also ; Latin: Ulysses, Ulixes), is a legendary Greek king of Ithaca and the hero of Homer's epic poem, the Odyssey. Odysseus also plays a key role in Homer's Iliad and other works in that same epic cycle.

Q472784.label: Hypermnestra
Q472784.description: daughter of Danaus in Greek mythology
Q472784.lead: In Greek mythology, Hypermnestra was by birth a Libyan princess and by marriage a queen of Argos. She is a daughter of King Danaus, and one of the 50 Danaids.

Q474854.label: Amphictyon
Q474854.description: son of Deucalion in Greek mythology
Q474854.lead: In Greek mythology, Amphictyon was a king of Thermopylae and later Athens. In one account, he was the ruler of Locris.

Q474888.label: Amphilochus
Q474888.lead: In Greek mythology, Amphilochus was an Argive hero and one of the Epigoni.

Q482096.label: Amymone
Q482096.description: daughter of Danaus in Greek mythology
Q482096.lead: In Greek mythology, Amymone was one of the 50 Danaids as a daughter of Danaus, king of Libya. As the "blameless" Danaid, her name identifies her as, perhaps, identical to Hypermnestra ("great wooing" or "high marriage"): the one Danaid who did not assassinate her husband on their wedding night.

Q48305.label: Euripides
Q48305.lead: Euripides was a Greek tragedian of classical Athens. Along with Aeschylus and Sophocles, he is one of the three authors of Greek tragedy whose name is ascribed to surviving plays.

Q48665.label: Enarete
Q48665.description: daughter of Deimachus in Greek mythology
Q48665.lead: In Greek mythology, Enarete, or Aenarete (Αἰναρέτη Ainarete), was a queen of Aeolia (i.e. Thessaly) and ancestor of the Aeolians.

Q486698.label: Omphale
Q486698.description: daughter of Iardanus, in Greek mythology
Q486698.lead: In Greek mythology, Omphale was princess of the kingdom of Lydia in Asia Minor. Diodorus Siculus provides the first appearance of the Omphale theme in literature, though Aeschylus was aware of the episode.

Q48774282.label: Astyoche
Q48774282.description: person from Greek mythology, daughter of Phylas

Q4891678.label: Dercynus
Q4891678.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q4891678.lead: In Greek mythology, Dercynus was a son of Poseidon and brother of Alebion (Ialebion). The two brothers engaged into battle with Heracles at Liguria of North-Western Italy.

Q495133.label: Atthis
Q495133.description: daughter of Cranaus in Greek mythology
Q495133.lead: In Greek mythology, Atthis or Attis (Ancient Greek: Ἄττις) was the eponymous heroine of Attica.

Q496595.label: Alcinous
Q496595.description: mythical character, King of the Phaeacians, son of Nausithous and brother of Rhexenor
Q496595.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcinous was a son of Nausithous and brother of Rhexenor. After the latter's death, he married his brother's daughter Arete who bore him Nausicaa, Halius, Clytoneus and Laodamas.

Q500739.label: Cecrops I
Q500739.lead: Cecrops was a legendary king of Attica which derived from him its name Cecropia, according to the Parian Chronicle having previously borne the name of Acte or Actice (from Actaeus). He was the founder and the first king of Athens itself though preceded in the region by the earth-born king Actaeus of Attica.

Q501667.label: Lycaon
Q501667.description: Greek mythical character, king of Arcadia, son of Pelasgus and Meliboea
Q501667.lead: In Greek mythology, Lycaon was a king of Arcadia who, in the most popular version of the myth, killed and cooked his son Nyctimus and served him to Zeus, to see whether the god was sufficiently all-knowing to recognize human flesh. Disgusted, Zeus transformed Lycaon into a wolf, while Nyctimus was restored to life.

Q502156.label: Pirithous
Q502156.description: son of Ixion in Greek mythology
Q502156.lead: Pirithous, in Greek mythology, was the King of the Lapiths of Larissa in Thessaly, as well as best friend to Theseus.

Q504076.label: Iolaos
Q504076.description: nephew of Heracles in Greek mythology
Q504076.lead: In Greek mythology, Iolaus was a Theban divine hero. He was famed for being Heracles's charioteer and squire, and for helping with some of his Labors, as well as for being one of the Argonauts.

Q506285.label: Eurybia
Q506285.lead: In Greek mythology, Eurybia, described as "[having] a heart of flint within her", was the daughter of Pontus and Gaia, consort to the Titan Crius, and mother of Astraeus, Perses, and Pallas. An older, relatively minor deity, her role in most mythology is as the ancestor of other gods, and she often plays no role in the mythology.

Q506550.label: Eteocles
Q506550.lead: In Greek mythology, Eteocles was a king of Thebes, the son of Oedipus and either Jocasta or Euryganeia. Oedipus killed his father Laius and married his mother without knowing his relationship to either.

Q508543.label: Aerope
Q508543.description: daughter of Catreus, the king of Crete
Q508543.lead: In Greek mythology, Aerope was a Cretan princess as the daughter of Catreus, king of Crete. She was the sister of Clymene, Apemosyne and Althaemenes.

Q512388.label: Androgeus
Q512388.lead: In Greek mythology, Androgeus or Androgeos was a Cretan prince as the son of King Minos.

Q514746.label: Xuthus
Q514746.lead: In Greek mythology, Xuthus was a Phthian prince who later became a king of Peloponnesus. He was the founder (through his sons) of the Achaean and Ionian nations.

Q51583754.label: Pelagon
Q51583754.description: Phocian of Greek mythology, with cows

Q518265.label: Aglaurus
Q518265.lead: Aglaurus or Agraulus (Ἄγραυλος, lit. 'living in the fields' or the 'rustic one') is a name attributed to three figures in Greek mythology. Aglaurus, the daughter of Actaeus, the first king of Attica.

Q532251.label: Syleus
Q532251.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q532251.lead: In Greek mythology, Syleus was a man of Aulis, Lydia killed by Heracles for his nefarious deeds. He was the father of Xenodoce.

Q541061.label: Alebion
Q541061.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q541061.lead: In Greek mythology, Alebion or Albion (Ἀλβίων) of Liguria, was a son of Poseidon and brother of Dercynus (also called Bergion or Ligys). In one source, Alebion was also known as Ialebion (Ἰαλεβίων).

Q542758.label: Styx
Q542758.description: Greek divinity of the river Styx
Q542758.lead: In Greek mythology, Styx, also called the River Styx, is a goddess and one of the rivers of the Greek Underworld.

Q548099.label: Eurynome
Q548099.lead: In Greek mythology Eurynome was an Oceanid and the mother of the Charites by Zeus.

Q5623747.label: Psamathe
Q5623747.lead: In Greek mythology, Psamathe is a Nereid, one of the fifty daughters of the sea god Nereus and the Oceanid Doris. By Aeacus, the king of Aegina, she is the mother of a son, Phocus.

Q568768.label: Erigone
Q568768.description: daughter of Icarius of Athens in Greek mythology
Q568768.lead: In Greek mythology, Erigone was the daughter of Icarius of Athens.

Q570434.label: Idomeneus
Q570434.description: Greek mythical character, King of Crete
Q570434.lead: In Greek mythology, Idomeneus was a Cretan king and commander who led the Cretan armies to the Trojan War, in eighty black ships. He was also one of the suitors of Helen, as well as a comrade of the Telamonian Ajax.

Q575252.label: Oxylus
Q575252.description: son of Haemon, mythical king of Elis
Q575252.lead: Oxylus, was a mythical king of Elis, who came from Aetolia and was son of Haemon (himself son of Thoas) or of Andraemon.

Q577245.label: Cycnus
Q577245.description: character in Greek mythology, son of Ares, killed by Heracles
Q577245.lead: In Greek mythology, Cycnus or Cygnus was a bloodthirsty and cruel man who dwelt either in Pagasae, Thessaly or by the river Echedorus in Macedonia.

Q578378.label: Aphareus
Q578378.description: Greek mythological character, son of Perieres
Q578378.lead: In Greek mythology, Aphareus was a Messenian king.

Q578888.label: Ceyx
Q578888.description: mythical son of Phosporus, husband of Alcyone
Q578888.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcyone (or dubiously Halcyone) and Ceyx (Ancient Greek: Κήυξ, romanized: Kḗux) were a wife and husband who incurred the wrath of the god Zeus for their romantic hubris.

Q591089.label: Alcmaeon
Q591089.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcmaeon, as one of the Epigoni, was the leader of the Argives who attacked Thebes, taking the city in retaliation for the deaths of their fathers, the Seven against Thebes, who died while attempting the same thing.

Q592348.label: Halirrhothius
Q592348.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q592348.lead: Halirrhothius was the Athenian son of Poseidon and Euryte or Bathycleia in Greek mythology. He was also called the son of Perieres and husband of Alcyone who bore him two sons, Serus and Alazygus.

Q599482.label: Tros
Q599482.description: ruler of Troy in Greek mythology
Q599482.lead: In Greek mythology, Tros was the founder of the kingdom of Troy, of which the city of Ilios, founded by his son Ilus took the same name, and the son of Erichthonius by Astyoche (daughter of the river god Simoeis) or of Ilus I, from whom he inherited the throne. Tros was the father of three sons: Ilus, Assaracus and Ganymede and two daughters, Cleopatra and Cleomestra.

Q599737.label: Marsyas
Q599737.lead: In Greek mythology, the satyr Marsyas is a central figure in two stories involving music: in one, he picked up the double oboe (aulos) that had been abandoned by Athena and played it; in the other, he challenged Apollo to a contest of music and lost his hide and life. Literary sources from antiquity often emphasize the hubris of Marsyas and the justice of his punishment.

Q602258.label: Melampus
Q602258.lead: In Greek mythology, Melampus was a legendary soothsayer and healer, originally of Pylos, who ruled at Argos. Melampus was the introducer of the worship of Dionysus, according to Herodotus, who asserted that his powers as a seer were derived from the Egyptians and that he could understand the language of animals.

Q605744.label: Asia
Q605744.lead: In Greek mythology, Asia was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, daughters of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-spouse Tethys. In some accounts, her mother was called Pompholyge and sister of Libye.

Q606422.label: Arcas
Q606422.description: son of Callisto in Greek mythology
Q606422.lead: In Greek mythology, Arcas was a hunter who became king of Arcadia. He was remembered for having taught people the arts of weaving and baking bread and for spreading agriculture to Arcadia.

Q607170.label: Achaeus
Q607170.description: Greek mythological figure, son of Xuthus
Q607170.lead: In Greek mythology, Achaeus or Achaios was a son of Xuthus and Creusa, and the brother of Ion as well as the grandson of Hellen. According to Pausanias, he was the father of Archander and Architeles, who travelled from Phthiotis to Argos and each married daughters of Danaus.

Q6072426.label: Periboea
Q6072426.description: daughter of Hipponous in Greek mythology

Q60794033.label: Hippolyte
Q60794033.lead: In Greek mythology, Hippolyte or Hippolyta was the name of the following characters: Hippolyte, one of the Hesperides and sister of Mapsaura and Thetis. Hippolyte, queen of the Amazons.

Q6081792.label: Polyphontes
Q6081792.description: king of Messenia in Greek mythology

Q6119921.label: Sandocus
Q6119921.description: son of Astynous in Greek mythology
Q6119921.lead: In Greek mythology, Sandocus or Sandacus (Σάνδακος) was the son of Astynous, the son of Phaethon.

Q616782.label: Cilix
Q616782.lead: Cilix was, according to Greek mythology, a Phoenician prince and the son of King Agenor and Telephassa or Argiope.

Q617753.label: Belus
Q617753.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q617753.lead: In Greek mythology, Belus was a king of Egypt and father of Aegyptus and Danaus and (usually) brother to Agenor. The wife of Belus has been named as Achiroe or Side (eponym of the Phoenician city of Sidon).

Q618175.label: Apemosyne
Q618175.description: daughter of Catreus in Greek mythology
Q618175.lead: In Greek mythology, Apemosyne was a Cretan princess as the daughter of King Catreus of Crete, the son of Minos. She had a brother Althaemenes, and two sisters, Aerope and Clymene.

Q618662.label: Apis
Q618662.description: king of Argos in Greek mythology
Q618662.lead: Apis was a king of Argos in Greek mythology.

Q622504.label: Thyestes
Q622504.description: King of Mycenae and brother of Atreus in Greek mythologie
Q622504.lead: In Greek mythology, Thyestes was a king of Olympia. Thyestes and his brother, Atreus, were exiled by their father for having murdered their half-brother, Chrysippus, in their desire for the throne of Olympia.

Q622781.label: Asopus
Q622781.lead: Asopus or Asopos is the name of four different rivers in Greece and one in Turkey. In Greek mythology, it was also the name of the gods of those rivers.

Q622809.label: Pyrrha
Q622809.description: daughter of Epimetheus and Pandora in Greek mythology
Q622809.lead: In Greek mythology, Pyrrha is the daughter of Epimetheus and Pandora, or of Prometheus.

Q624551.label: Nephele
Q624551.description: cloud goddess, wife of Athamas and mother of Phrixus and Helle
Q624551.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Nephele called Nebula by Latin authors, is the name of two figures associated with clouds, who figure respectively in the stories of Ixion and in the story of Phrixus and his sister Helle.

Q633120.label: Pandrosus
Q633120.description: daughter of Cecrops I in Greek mythology
Q633120.lead: Pandrosos or Pandrosus was known in Greek myth as one of the three daughters of Cecrops I, the first king of Athens, and Aglaurus, daughter of King Actaeus.

Q636796.label: Temenus
Q636796.description: son of Aristomachus, in Greek mythology
Q636796.lead: In Greek mythology, Temenus was a son of Aristomachus and brother of Cresphontes and Aristodemus. Temenus was a great-great-grandson of Heracles and helped lead the fifth and final attack on Mycenae in the Peloponnese.

Q637955.label: Neleus
Q637955.description: mythical son of Poseidon or Cretheus and father of Nestor
Q637955.lead: Neleus was a mythological king of Pylos. In some accounts, he was also counted as an Argonaut instead of his son, Nestor.

Q638578.label: Helle
Q638578.lead: Helle, sometimes also called Athamantis (Ancient Greek: Ἀθαμαντίς, "daughter of Athamas"), was a character in Greek mythology who figured prominently in the story of Jason and the Argonauts. Helle is known for giving her name to the strait of Hellespont ("sea of Helle"), into which she fell while crossing it on the back of a flying golden ram with her brother Phrixus—the same flying ram from which the Golden Fleece derived.

Q6395637.label: Keuthonymos
Q6395637.lead: Ceuthonymus or Keuthonymos is a spirit in Greek mythology who is the father of Menoites (or Menoetes, Menoetius). Ceuthonymus is a mysterious daimon or spirit of the underworld, who lives in the realm of Hades.

Q641065.label: Phineus
Q641065.description: son of Agenor in Greek mythology
Q641065.lead: In Greek mythology, Phineus was a king of Salmydessus in Thrace and seer, who appears in accounts of the Argonauts' voyage. Some accounts make him a king in Paphlagonia or in Arcadia.

Q641286.label: Rhodos
Q641286.description: Goddess of Rhodes in Greek mythology
Q641286.lead: In Greek mythology, Rhodos/Rhodus or Rhode (Ancient Greek: Ῥόδη, romanized: Rhódē), was the goddess and personification of the island of Rhodes and a wife of the sun god Helios.

Q643504.label: Cephalus
Q643504.description: son of Deioneus and beloved of Eos in Greek mythology
Q643504.lead: In Greek mythology, Cephalus or Kephalos was the son of Deion, the ruler of Phocis, and Diomede.

Q644604.label: Proetus
Q644604.lead: In Greek mythology, Proetus, the son of Abas, was a king of Argos and Tiryns.

Q644921.label: Erichthonius
Q644921.lead: In Greek mythology, King Erichthonius was a legendary early ruler of ancient Athens. According to some myths, he was autochthonous (born of the soil, or Earth) and adopted or raised by the goddess Athena.

Q646049.label: Hyades
Q646049.description: nymphs associated with rain in Greek mythology
Q646049.lead: In Greek mythology, the Hyades are a sisterhood of nymphs that bring rain.

Q649476.label: Argus
Q649476.description: mythological Greek character, king and eponym of Argos
Q649476.lead: In Greek mythology, Argus was the king and eponym of Argos.

Q649624.label: Phoroneus
Q649624.description: son of Inachus in Greek mythology
Q649624.lead: In Greek mythology, Phoroneus was a culture-hero of the Argolid, fire-bringer, law giver, and primordial king of Argos.

Q653681.label: Alcyoneus
Q653681.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcyoneus or Alkyoneus was a traditional opponent of the hero Heracles. He was usually considered to be one of the Gigantes (Giants), the offspring of Gaia born from the blood of the castrated Uranus.

Q654257.label: Tiphys
Q654257.lead: In Greek mythology, Tiphys was the helmsman of the Argonauts.

Q656881.label: Tiresias
Q656881.lead: In Greek mythology, Tiresias was a blind prophet of Apollo in Thebes, famous for clairvoyance and for being transformed into a woman for seven years. He was the son of the shepherd Everes and the nymph Chariclo.

Q656887.label: Tityos
Q656887.lead: Tityos or Tityus is a giant from Greek mythology. The son of Zeus and the mortal Elara, Tityos tried to rape the goddess Leto, a former lover of Zeus and the mother of the twin gods Artemis and Apollo.

Q657174.label: Talos
Q657174.lead: In Greek mythology, Talos, also spelled Talus or Talon (Greek: Τάλων, Tálōn), was a man of bronze who protected Crete from pirates and invaders. Despite the popular idea that he was a giant, no ancient source states this explicitly.

Q658523.label: Hermione
Q658523.description: daughter of Menelaus and Helen of Troy
Q658523.lead: In Greek mythology, Hermione was the daughter of Menelaus, king of Sparta, and his wife, Helen of Troy. Prior to the Trojan War, Hermione had been betrothed by Tyndareus, her grandfather, to her cousin Orestes, son of her uncle, Agamemnon.

Q660924.label: Perses
Q660924.lead: In Greek mythology, Perses is the son of the Titan Crius and Eurybia, and thus brother to Astraeus and Pallas. Ancient tradition records very little of Perses other than his marriage and offspring, his role largely being genealogical, existing merely to provide a parentage for other, more important figures.

Q666525.label: Aristodemus
Q666525.description: one of the Heracleidae in Greek mythology
Q666525.lead: In Greek mythology, Aristodemus was one of the Heracleidae, son of Aristomachus and brother of Cresphontes and Temenus. He was a great-great-grandson of Heracles and helped lead the fifth and final attack on Mycenae in the Peloponnese.

Q668054.label: Talaus
Q668054.description: son of Bias in Greek mythology
Q668054.lead: In Greek mythology, Talaus was the king of Argos and one of the Argonauts. He was the son of Bias (or Perialces) and Pero, and brother of Arëius and Leodocus.

Q675699.label: Epaphus
Q675699.description: mythical character, son of Zeus and Io
Q675699.lead: In Greek mythology, Epaphus, also called Apis or Munantius was a son of Zeus and king of Egypt.

Q679716.label: Cychreus
Q679716.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q679716.lead: In Greek mythology, Cychreus was a legendary king of Salamis Island. He was the son of the god Poseidon and the nymph Salamis.

Q690613.label: Tlepolemus
Q690613.lead: In Greek mythology, Tlepolemus was the leader of the Rhodian forces in the Trojan War.

Q697942.label: Amycus
Q697942.description: in Greek mythology, the king of the Bebryces, a mythical people in Bithynia
Q697942.lead: In Greek mythology, Amykos, Latinized as Amycus, was the king of the Bebryces, a mythical people in Bithynia.

Q6994910.label: Nephalion
Q6994910.description: Greek mythical character, son of Minos
Q6994910.lead: In Greek mythology, Nephalion was one of the four sons of Minos, who lived on the Greek island of Paros. Nephalion and his brothers Eurymedon, Khryses, and Philolaus rebelled against Herakles and murdered two sailors from one of his vessels that had washed up ashore on the rocks of Paros.

Q725286.label: Coronis
Q725286.description: goddess from Greek mythology: princess, daughter of Phlegyas, lover of Ischys and Apollo, mother of Asclepius; killed by Apollon and Artemis
Q725286.lead: In Greek mythology, Coronis is a Thessalian princess and a lover of the god Apollo. She was the daughter of Cleophema and Phlegyas, king of the Lapiths.

Q725527.label: Calchas
Q725527.lead: Calchas is an Argive mantis, or seer, in Greek mythology. Calchas appears in the opening scenes of the Iliad and also has a long literary history after Homer.

Q733985.label: Haemon
Q733985.description: Greek mythical character, son of Creon
Q733985.lead: In Greek mythology, Haemon was the son of Creon and Eurydice, and thus brother of Menoeceus (Megareus), Lycomedes, Megara, Pyrrha and Henioche. The various sources of his myth present differing and contradictory versions of his story.

Q735623.label: Inachus
Q735623.description: river deity and king of the Argolid
Q735623.lead: In Greek mythology, Inachus or Inachos was the first king of Argos. He was one of the three thousand sons of Oceanus and Tethys.

Q737306.label: Tithonus
Q737306.description: prince of Troy loved by Eos in Greek mythology
Q737306.lead: In Greek mythology, Tithonus was the lover of Eos, Goddess of the Dawn. He was a prince of Troy, the son of King Laomedon by the Naiad Strymo (Στρυμώ).

Q738007.label: Melicertes
Q738007.lead: In Greek mythology, Melicertes, later called Palaemon or Palaimon (Παλαίμων), was a Boeotian prince as the son of King Athamas and Ino, daughter of King Cadmus of Thebes. He was the brother of Learchus.

Q7382381.label: Chione
Q7382381.description: mythological Greek character, daughter of Boreas
Q7382381.lead: In Greek mythology, Chione is a mortal woman, the daughter of Boreas, the god of the north wind, and the princess Orithyia, a daughter of Erechtheus, the king of Athens. In the only myth concerning her, Chione sleeps with the sea-god Poseidon and bears him a son, Eumolpus, but in fear of her father's wrath she casts the infant into the sea.

Q738862.label: Iphicles
Q738862.description: son of Amphitryon in Greek mythology
Q738862.lead: In Greek mythology, Iphicles, also called Iphiclus, was the maternal half-twin brother of Heracles and one of the Calydonian boar hunters.

Q739359.label: Assaracus
Q739359.description: son of Tros in Greek mythology
Q739359.lead: In Greek mythology, Assaracus was a king of Dardania.

Q740468.label: Busiris
Q740468.description: king of Egypt in Greek mythology
Q740468.lead: In Greek mythology, Busiris was an Egyptian king of the central Delta who was killed by Heracles.

Q741155.label: Nycteus
Q741155.lead: In Greek mythology, Nycteus was a king of Thebes. His rule began after the death of Polydorus, and ended when he was succeeded by his brother Lycus.

Q743482.label: Phrixus
Q743482.description: son of Athamas in Greek mythology
Q743482.lead: In Greek mythology Phrixus was the son of Athamas, king of Boeotia, and Nephele (a goddess of clouds). He was the older brother of Helle and the father of Argus, Phrontis, Melas and Cytisorus by Chalciope (Iophassa), daughter of Aeetes, king of Colchis.

Q744147.label: Iole
Q744147.lead: In Greek mythology, Iole was the daughter of King Eurytus of Oechalia. According to the brief epitome in the Bibliotheca, Eurytus had a beautiful young daughter named Iole who was eligible for marriage.

Q748144.label: Idmon
Q748144.description: son of Abas in Greek mythology
Q748144.lead: In Greek mythology, Idmon was an Argonaut seer.

Q749966.label: Oeneus
Q749966.lead: In Greek mythology, Oeneus was a Calydonian king. He was the first who received a vine-plant from Dionysos.

Q750580.label: Pittheus
Q750580.description: son of Pelops in Greek mythology
Q750580.lead: In Greek mythology, Pittheus was the king of Troezen, city in Argolis, which he had named after his brother Troezen.

Q752330.label: Astydameia
Q752330.description: wife of Acastus, queen of Iolcus
Q752330.lead: In Greek mythology, Astydamia, also called Hippolyta and sometimes simply identified as Cretheis in a patronymic manner (Κρηθηίς, lit. 'the daughter of Cretheus'), is a princess and then queen of the ancient Greek city of Iolcus in Thessaly, the daughter of Cretheus and wife of Acastus. Astydamia fell in love with Peleus of Phthia and tried to seduce him during his short stay at Iolcus, but when her efforts failed she accused him of assault to her husband Acastus, an act that would make Peleus forever an enemy to the royal couple and their city.

Q753902.label: Ismene
Q753902.lead: In Greek mythology, Ismene was a Theban princess. She was the daughter and half-sister of Oedipus, king of Thebes, daughter and granddaughter of Jocasta, and sister of Antigone, Eteocles, and Polynices.

Q754835.label: Catreus
Q754835.description: king of Crete and a son of Minos and Pasiphaë
Q754835.lead: In Greek mythology, Catreus, also spelled Katreus, was the eldest son of Minos and Pasiphaë, and Minos's successor as king of Crete. Catreus had one son, Althaemenes, and three daughters, Apemosyne, Aerope and Clymene.

Q7595427.label: Cyllene
Q7595427.lead: In Greek mythology, Cyllene, also spelled Kyllene, is the Naiad nymph and the personification of Mount Cyllene in Arcadia, the region in Greece where the god of travellers and shepherds Hermes was born and brought up. In some versions Cyllene is said to have been Hermes' nurse and caretaker while he was growing up.

Q760213.label: Auge
Q760213.description: daughter of Aleus in Greek mythology
Q760213.lead: In Greek mythology, Auge, was the daughter of Aleus the king of Tegea in Arcadia, and the virgin priestess of Athena Alea. She was also the mother of the hero Telephus by Heracles.

Q765456.label: Laodamas
Q765456.description: son of Eteocles in Greek mythology

Q768822.label: Thestius
Q768822.description: son of Agenor in Greek mythology
Q768822.lead: In Greek mythology, Thestius was a king of Pleuronians in Aetolia. He is not to be confused with Thespius, who was sometimes referred to as "Thestius".

Q7707084.label: Teutamides
Q7707084.lead: In Greek mythology, Teutamides or Teutamus (Tεύταμoς) was a king of Larissa, Thessaly. He was the son of Amyntor and a great-grandson of Pelasgus; his own son was Nanas.

Q771241.label: Polydectes
Q771241.lead: In Greek mythology, King Polydectes is a king of the island of Seriphos in the Cyclades. Polydectes was the ruler of the island when the Argive princess Danaë and her infant son Perseus washed ashore, having been cast away into the sea by Danaë's father Acrisius, who was afraid that his daughter's son would kill him.

Q771366.label: Myrrha
Q771366.description: daughter of Cinyras in Greek mythology
Q771366.lead: Myrrha, also known as Smyrna (Ancient Greek: Σμύρνα, romanized: Smýrna), is the mother of Adonis in Greek mythology. She was transformed into a myrrh tree after having coitus with her father, and gave birth — in tree form — to Adonis.

Q775296.label: Hypsipyle
Q775296.description: queen of Lemnos, granddaughter of Ariadne and Dionysos in Greek mythology
Q775296.lead: In Greek mythology, Hypsipyle was a queen of Lemnos, and the daughter of King Thoas of Lemnos, and the granddaughter of Dionysus and Ariadne. When the women of Lemnos killed all the males on the island, Hypsipyle saved her father Thoas.

Q776139.label: Semele
Q776139.description: mother of Dionysus in Greek mythology
Q776139.lead: In Greek mythology, Semele, or Thyone (Ancient Greek: Θυώνη, romanized: Thyṓnē), was the youngest daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, and the mother of Dionysus by Zeus (her own great-grandfather). Certain elements of the cult of Dionysus and Semele came from the Phrygians.

Q784528.label: Autesion
Q784528.lead: In Greek mythology, Autesion, was a king of Thebes. He was the son of Tisamenus, the grandson of Thersander and Demonassa and the great-grandson of Polynices and Argea.

Q7877819.label: Lynceus
Q7877819.description: son of Aegyptus in Greek mythology
Q7877819.lead: In Greek mythology, Lynceus was a prince of Egypt and king of Argos, succeeding Danaus on the throne. Through his marriage to the Danaid Hypermnestra, he began the Danaid Dynasty that led to Perseus, hero and legendary founder of Mycenae.

Q793088.label: Benthesikyme
Q793088.lead: In Greek mythology, Benthesikyme or Benthesicyme was, according to the mythographer Apollodorus, a daughter of Poseidon and Amphitrite, and the foster mother of Eumolpus. After Chione slept with Poseidon, she gave birth to Eumolpus, but, to avoid the detection of her father, she threw the infant into the sea.

Q79999.label: Uranus
Q79999.description: primordial Greek deity, god of the Sky; one of the Greek primordial deities
Q79999.lead: In Greek mythology, Uranus, sometimes written Ouranos (Ancient Greek: Οὐρανός, lit. 'sky', [uːranós]), is the personification of the sky and one of the Greek primordial deities. According to Hesiod, Uranus was the son and husband of Gaia (Earth), with whom he fathered the first generation of Titans.

Q82732.label: Aeneas
Q82732.description: Trojan hero, son of Anchises and Aphrodite
Q82732.lead: Aeneas was a Trojan hero in Greco-Roman mythology, the son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the Greek goddess Aphrodite (equivalent to the Roman Venus). His father was a first cousin of King Priam of Troy (both being great-grandsons of Tros, founder of Troy), making Aeneas a second cousin to Priam's children (such as Hector and Paris).

Q830706.label: Hyrnetho
Q830706.description: daughter of Temenus in Greek mythology
Q830706.lead: In Greek mythology, Hyrnetho was a daughter of Temenus, and the wife of Deiphontes, by whom she became mother of Antimenes, Xanthippus, Argeius, and Orsobia. Temenus favored his daughter Hyrnetho and her husband Deiphontes more than his sons, Hyrnetho's brothers, and planned on making Deiphontes his heir.

Q83160.label: Prometheus
Q83160.description: Titan, culture hero, and trickster figure in Greek mythology who defied the gods; son of Iapetus
Q83160.lead: In Greek mythology, Prometheus is a Titan who is responsible for creating and aiding humanity in its earliest days. He defied the Olympian gods by stealing fire from them and giving it to humanity.

Q83223.label: Asclepius
Q83223.lead: Asclepius is a hero and god of medicine in ancient Greek religion and mythology. He is the son of Apollo and Coronis, or Arsinoe, or of Apollo alone.

Q833806.label: Capaneus
Q833806.description: son of Hipponous in Greek mythology
Q833806.lead: In Greek mythology, Capaneus was a son of Hipponous and either Astynome (daughter of Talaus) or Laodice (daughter of Iphis), and husband of Evadne, with whom he fathered Sthenelus. Some call his wife Ianeira.

Q833826.label: Nauplius
Q833826.description: king of Nauplia, son of Poseidon in Greek mythology

Q83496.label: Cerberus
Q83496.description: three-headed dog that guards the underworld in Greek mythology
Q83496.lead: In Greek mythology, Cerberus, often referred to as the hound of Hades, is a multi-headed dog that guards the gates of the underworld to prevent the dead from leaving. He was the offspring of the monsters Echidna and Typhon, and was usually described as having three heads, a serpent for a tail, and snakes protruding from his body.

Q836140.label: Euryale
Q836140.description: mythical character; second eldest of the Gorgons
Q836140.lead: In Greek mythology, Stheno and Euryale ( yuu-RY-ə-lee; Ancient Greek: Εὐρυάλη, romanized: Euryálē, lit. 'far-roaming') were two of the three sister Gorgons, the third being Medusa, who were able to turn anyone who looked at them to stone. Unlike the mortal Medusa, both Stheno and Euryale were immortal.

Q836311.label: Phocus
Q836311.lead: In Greek mythology, Phocus, was a prince of Aegina and son of Aeacus and Psamathe.

Q842435.label: Arion
Q842435.lead: In Greek mythology, Arion or Areion, is a divinely-bred, fabulously fast, black-maned horse. He saved the life of Adrastus, king of Argos, during the war of the Seven against Thebes.

Q843335.label: Sinis
Q843335.lead: In Greek mythology, Sinis was a bandit killed by Theseus on his way to Athens.

Q845112.label: Enceladus
Q845112.lead: In Greek mythology, Enceladus was one of the Giants, the offspring of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky). Enceladus was the traditional opponent of Athena during the Gigantomachy, the war between the Giants and the gods, and was said to be buried under Mount Etna in Sicily.

Q847005.label: Labdacus
Q847005.lead: In Greek mythology, Labdacus was the only son of Polydorus and a king of Thebes. Labdacus was a grandson of Thebes's founder, Cadmus.

Q847268.label: Hyllus
Q847268.description: son of Heracles and Deianira in Greek mythology
Q847268.lead: In Greek mythology, Hyllus or Hyllas (Ὕλλᾱς, Hyllas) was a son of Heracles and Deianira and the husband of Iole.

Q849438.label: Iasion
Q849438.lead: In Greek mythology, Iasion or Iasus (Ancient Greek: Ἴασος, romanized: Íasos), also called Eetion (Ancient Greek: Ἠετίων, romanized: Ēetíōn), was the founder of the mystic rites on the island of Samothrace.

Q849647.label: Briareus
Q849647.lead: In Greek mythology, the Hecatoncheires, also called Hundred-Handers or Centimanes (Latin: Centimani), were three monstrous giants, of enormous size and strength, each with fifty heads and one hundred arms. They were individually named Cottus (the furious), Briareus (or Aegaeon, the sea goat) and Gyges (or Gyes, the long-limbed).

Q850192.label: Dirce
Q850192.description: daughter of Ismenus in Greek mythology
Q850192.lead: Dirce was a queen of Thebes as the wife of Lycus in Greek mythology.

Q852301.label: Chryses
Q852301.description: mythical son of Minos and priest of Apollo
Q852301.lead: In Greek mythology, Chryses was a Trojan priest of Apollo at Chryse, near the city of Troy.

Q853014.label: Thamyris
Q853014.lead: In Greek mythology, Thamyris was a Thracian singer. He is notable in Greek mythology for reportedly having been in love with Hyacinth before the latter's relationship with Apollo and having been the first mortal male to have loved another male.

Q853437.label: Telephassa
Q853437.lead: Telephassa, also spelled Telephaassa (Τηλεφάασσα) and Telephe (Τηλέφη), is a lunar epithet in Greek mythology that is sometimes substituted for Argiope the wife of Agenor, according to his name a "leader of men" in Phoenicia, and mother of Cadmus.

Q853462.label: Ion son of Xuthus
Q853462.lead: According to Greek mythology, Ion was the eponymous ancestor of the Ionians.

Q855509.label: Bias
Q855509.lead: In Greek mythology, Bias, was one of the three kings of Argos when the kingdom was divided into three domains. The other kings were his brother Melampus and Anaxagoras.

Q858663.label: Electra
Q858663.description: one of the Pleiades in Greek mythology
Q858663.lead: In Greek mythology, Electra was one of the Pleiades, the seven daughters of Atlas and Pleione. She lived on the island of Samothrace.

Q858671.label: Oenone
Q858671.description: nymph of Greek mythology, wife of Paris
Q858671.lead: In Greek mythology, Oenone was the first wife of Paris of Troy, whom he abandoned for Helen. Oenone was also the ancient name of an island, which was later named after Aegina, daughter of the river god Asopus.

Q86805.label: Geryon
Q86805.description: mythical king of far western Mediterranean
Q86805.lead: In Greek mythology, Geryon was a fearsome giant who dwelt on the island Erytheia of the mythic Hesperides in the far west of the Mediterranean. A more literal-minded later generation of Greeks associated the region with Tartessos in southern Iberia.

Q869665.label: Cretheus
Q869665.description: in Greek mythology, king and founder of Iolcus

Q878184.label: Teucer
Q878184.lead: In Greek mythology, Teucer, was the son of King Telamon of Salamis Island and his second wife Hesione, daughter of King Laomedon of Troy. He fought alongside his half-brother, Ajax, in the Trojan War and is the legendary founder of the city of Salamis on Cyprus.

Q878246.label: Cinyras
Q878246.description: mythical founder of the city of Paphos in Greek mythology
Q878246.lead: In Greek mythology, Cinyras was a famous hero and king of Cyprus. Accounts vary significantly as to his genealogy and provide a variety of stories concerning him; in many sources he is associated with the cult of Aphrodite on Cyprus, and Adonis, a consort of Aphrodite, is mentioned as his son.

Q894066.label: Borus
Q894066.description: son of Perieres in Greek mythology

Q903606.label: Delphyne
Q903606.lead: In Greek mythology, Delphyne is the name given, by some accounts, to the monstrous serpent killed by Apollo at Delphi. Although, in Hellenistic and later accounts, the Delphic monster slain by Apollo is usually said to be the male serpent Python, in the earliest known account of this story, the Homeric Hymn to Apollo (6th century BC), the god kills a nameless she-serpent (drakaina), subsequently called Delphyne.

Q905409.label: Dictys
Q905409.description: mythic character, fisherman and brother of King Polydectes
Q905409.lead: Dictys was a name attributed to four men in Greek mythology. Dictys, a fisherman and brother of King Polydectes of Seriphos, both being the sons of Magnes and a Naiad, or of Peristhenes and Androthoe, or else of Poseidon and Cerebia.

Q912772.label: Deiphontes
Q912772.description: son of Antimachus in Greek mythology
Q912772.lead: Deiphontes was king of Argos. He was a son of Antimachus, and husband of Hyrnetho, the daughter of Temenus the Heracleide, by whom he became the father of Antimenes, Xanthippus, Argeius, and Orsobia.

Q912904.label: Alcyone
Q912904.description: Greek mythological figure; daughter of Aeolus
Q912904.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcyone (or dubiously Halcyone) and Ceyx (Ancient Greek: Κήυξ, romanized: Kḗux) were a wife and husband who incurred the wrath of the god Zeus for their romantic hubris.

Q916442.label: Telephus
Q916442.lead: In Greek mythology, Telephus was the son of Heracles and Auge, who was the daughter of king Aleus of Tegea. He was adopted by Teuthras, the king of Mysia, in Asia Minor, whom he succeeded as king.

Q922330.label: Lichas
Q922330.lead: In Greek mythology, Lichas was Heracles' servant, who brought the poisoned shirt from Deianira to Hercules because of Deianira's jealousy of Iole, which killed him.

Q927322.label: Admete
Q927322.description: daughter of Eurystheus in Greek mythology
Q927322.lead: Admete or Admeta, was in Greek mythology, a Mycenaean princess. She was the daughter of King Eurystheus and Antimache and sister to Alexander, Iphimedon, Eurybius, Mentor, Perimedes and possibly, Eurypylus.

Q928411.label: Cranaus
Q928411.lead: In Greek mythology, Cranaus or Kranaos was the second King of Athens, succeeding Cecrops I.

Q929768.label: Megara
Q929768.description: mythical wife of Heracles and daughter of Creon
Q929768.lead: In Greek mythology, Megara was a Theban princess and the first wife of the hero Heracles.

Q93172.label: Gaia
Q93172.description: Greek primordial deity, the personification of the Earth
Q93172.lead: In Greek mythology, Gaia, also spelled Gaea, is the personification of Earth. She is the mother of Uranus (Sky), with whom she conceived the Titans (themselves parents of many of the Olympian gods), the Cyclopes, and the Giants, as well as of Pontus (Sea), from whose union she bore the primordial sea gods.

Q932325.label: Marpessa
Q932325.lead: In Greek mythology, Marpessa was an Aetolian princess and a granddaughter of Ares.

Q9336298.label: Side
Q9336298.description: wife of Orion in Greek mythology
Q9336298.lead: In ancient Greek and Roman mythology, Side is a little-known figure, the first wife of the great hunter Orion. Side challenged the goddess Hera in beauty so her punishment was to be thrown into Hades, the Underworld.

Q937216.label: Oenopion
Q937216.description: mythical character, son of Ariadne with Dionysus or Theseus
Q937216.lead: In Greek mythology, Oenopion was a legendary king of Chios, and was said to have brought winemaking to the island, which was assigned to him by Rhadamanthys.

Q939149.label: Eurytus
Q939149.lead: Eurytus of Oechalia (Οἰχαλίᾱ, Oikhalíā), Thessaly, was a skillful archer of Greek mythology who was even said to have instructed Heracles in the art of using the bow.

Q94066.label: Eileithyia
Q94066.description: Greek goddess of childbirth and midwifery
Q94066.lead: Eileithyia or Ilithyia was the Greek goddess of childbirth and midwifery, and the daughter of Zeus and Hera. In the cave of Amnisos (Crete) she was related with the annual birth of the divine child, and her cult is connected with Enesidaon (the earth shaker), who was the chthonic aspect of the god Poseidon.

Q94072.label: Autonoë
Q94072.lead: In Greek mythology, Autonoë was a Theban princess as the eldest daughter of Cadmus, founder of Thebes in Boeotia, and the goddess Harmonia. She was the wife of Aristaeus and mother of Actaeon and possibly Macris.

Q952188.label: Thespius
Q952188.description: legendary founder and king of Thespiae, Boeotia
Q952188.lead: In Greek mythology, Thespius or Thestius (Ancient Greek: Θέστιος, romanized: Théstios) was a legendary founder and king of Thespiae, Boeotia. His life account is considered part of Greek mythology.

Q960237.label: Eurysthenes
Q960237.lead: Eurysthenes was king of Sparta and one of the Heracleidae in Greek mythology. He was a son of Aristodemus and Argia, daughter of Autesion.

Q976463.label: Hippomedon
Q976463.description: son of Talaus and one of Seven Against Thebes in Greek mythology
Q976463.lead: In Greek mythology, Hippomedon was one of the Seven against Thebes. He lived near the lake Lerna in Peloponessus; the foundations of his house on Mount Pontinus at Lerna were shown in Pausanias' times.

Q978079.label: Harmonia
Q978079.description: ancient Greek goddess of harmony and concord, spouse of Cadmus; her opposite is Eris
Q978079.lead: In Greek mythology, Harmonia is the goddess of harmony and concord. She is traditionally the daughter of Aphrodite, the goddess of love, and Ares, the god of war.

Q979627.label: Orseis
Q979627.lead: In Greek mythology, Orseïs was the water-nymph (Naiad) of a spring in Thessalia, Greece, and the mythical ancestor of the Greeks. According to M. L. West, her name may have been corrupt for "Othryis", who he suggests was a nymph of Mount Othrys.

Q981302.label: Amphoterus
Q981302.description: son of Alcmaeon in Greek mythology
Q981302.lead: In Greek mythology, Amphoterus was the son of Alcmaeon by Callirrhoe (daughter of the river god Achelous), and brother of Acarnan.
